headline: Approved three FY '27 budget transfers; the 617 Lexington Street transformer project needs an additional $290,874.39.
summary: Union members asked for a fair contract, and a parent asked when families will see the high school schedule options. Calendar survey results on school days and religious holidays were shared. Enrollment was reported at 5,450 students.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including the October 21, 2026 minutes, personnel changes, and three donations; all in favor.
Provided the School Committee with the full district calendar survey data; all in favor.
Forwarded the three high school schedule questions raised during public comment to WHS Principal Dr. Conard to be answered; all in favor.
Tabled the School Committee Subcommittee Meetings matter to the next meeting; all in favor.
Approved the three FY '27 account transfers; all in favor.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant; all in favor.

 The regular meeting of the Waltham School Committee convened at 5:31pm. Present 
 were Ms. Wong-Bigelow, Mrs. AlJammal, Mrs. Coleman, Mayor McCarthy, Mr. 
 Tarallo, and Mr. Zanghi.  Ms. DeJoannis was not present.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to move to 
 Executive Session at 5:32pm to conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective 
 bargaining with the WSSA and / or to conduct negotiations with the WSSA; to 
 conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the WSAA and / 
 or to conduct negotiations with the WSAA; to conduct strategy sessions with respect 
 to collective bargaining with the Waltham School MIS Technicians and / or to conduct 
 negotiations with the Waltham School MIS Technicians; to conduct strategy sessions 
 with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham School Department Food 
 Service Workers and to conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective 
 bargaining with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers Association and/or to 
 conduct negotiations with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers Association, to 
 include Attorney Jonathan Atwater, Superintendent Dr. Mendonsa, and HR 
 Administrator Kate Peretz, and return to the regular meeting at 7:00 pm.  All in favor. 
 The School Committee reconvened at 7:01pm.  Present were Mr. Zanghi, Mrs. 
 Coleman, Mrs. AlJammal, Ms. DeJoannis, Ms. Wong-Bigelow, and Mayor McCarthy. 
 Mr. Tarallo was not present.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 The Committee recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to move item 
 2 out of order.  All in favor. 
 Waltham High School students John McCalla and Daniela Reyes shared updates 
 from Waltham High: the Cheerleaders, boys soccer, football, and field hockey teams 
 have all made the tournament for the fall season; Legally Blonde performances are in 
 two weeks; Multicultural Night is Friday; Health Assist clinics are underway; new 
 student officers were elected for the sophomore, junior and senior classes, and the 
 weekly Hawks news broadcasts have resumed. 
 WSSA members Linda Spruce, Karen Lawn, Lisa Burke, Mary Jo Nash, and Krissy 
 Scheufele all addressed the Committee to again request a fair and equitable 
 contract.  They advised they are committed to WPS, they work every day but want 
 their value recognized, and are tired of feeling invisible.  Ms. Scheufele reviewed 
 salary increases for nonunion executive / administrative assistants as well as 
 administrators noting funds appear to be available for some employees but not 
 others.  She requested her handout be included as part of the record. 
 Nicole Piche-Nicholas, a WHS parent, advised the community still has not received 
 the new schedule options being considered by the WHS Schedule committee.  She 
 added that no parents or caregivers are on the committee despite her repeated 
 requests to participate and therefore, the School Committee members, as elected 
 officials, should be the caregivers’ voice.  She specifically requested answers to three

 Dr. Mendonsa shared the feedback received from the 868 staff and family members 
 who responded to the recent district calendar survey.  In response to the question 
 about changing having school on the Friday before Labor Day weekend instead of on 
 the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, 50.3% of respondents voted to keep the 
 existing schedule, 36.5% voted to make this change and 13.1% had no preference. 
 In response to the question about having school on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and 
 Good Friday, 40.7% of people voted to continue not having school on these days, 
 34% indicated they would like school to be open on these religious holidays, and the 
 remaining 25.3% advised they were comfortable with either option. 
 The superintendent then shared some of the additional feedback received relative to 
 religious holidays, the start / end of the school year, the first day of kindergarten, and 
 early release days.  A short conversation followed about religious holidays, staff 
 coverage and impact on students. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Ms. Wong-Bigelow, seconded by Mrs. Coleman, to provide 
 the School Committee with the full district calendar survey data.  All in favor. 
 The monthly district enrollment report confirmed enrollment has stabilized at 5,45  0 
 students in Waltham Public Schools.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to hear from 
 all off-Committee members.  All in favor. 
 Northeast Elementary School’s principal Mary Ellen Tenaglia and Assistant Principal 
 Kelly McAvoy shared the school’s recent MCAS results showing substantial progress 
 toward targets is being made by students.  They advised the school’s chronic 
 absenteeism rate has decreased.  Student enrollment has also been decreasing over 
 the last few years.  The addition of a family liaison and another School Adjustment 
 Counselor to Northeast has been very beneficial to students and their families. 
 The school’s Student Learning goal was identified as, “Northeast Elementary School 
 students will monitor their own understanding and complete academic tasks with 
 greater independence through the use of Learning Objectives, Criteria for Success, 
 and Teacher Feedback.” 
 Mrs. Tenaglia announced the Professional Practice goal for this year is, “Northeast 
 Elementary School educators will intentionally post, unpack, and revisit Learning 
 Objectives, establish and share clear Criteria for Success, and provide timely, 
 specific, and actionable Feedback in order for students to monitor their own 
 understanding and complete academic tasks with greater independence.” 
 Northeast’s School Culture goal is, “Northeast Elementary School will create 
 opportunities for students to develop positive relationships, build social-emotional 
 skills, and experience a sense of belonging through routines and daily SEL 
 instruction, intentional inclusive and supportive learning environments, and 
 opportunities for student self-reflection.” 
 The principal  shared the plans to achieve each of the stated goals during the year 
 and also how data will be tracked and progress monitored. 
 Whittemore Elementary’s principal Dave Sweder, accompanied by Assistant Principal 
 Liz Uccello, shared the school’s improvement in its accountability percentile and 
 MCAS and Dibels scores.  They confirmed they have seen positive improvements in 
 high focus areas and will continue to make these a priority. 
 Mr. Sweder indicated the school’s Professional Practice goal is, “Whittemore 
 educators will build their capacity to effectively maintain high quality Tier 1 instruction 
 while also providing meaningful, targeted practice to meet ALL students’ needs 
 during WIN block.” 
 Whittemore’s Student Learning goal is, “Whittemore students will demonstrate 
 consistent, positive behavioral choices across all school settings as a result of 
 explicit, building-wide instruction aligned to the BEST framework.” 
 The Family / Caregiver goal for this year is, “Whittemore families will strengthen our 
 school community by building relationships and engaging in shared learning 
 experiences across cultural and linguistic groups.” 
 The principal detailed the steps that will be taken in order to meet these goals and 
 how progress will be tracked during the school year.

 Dr. Ricardo Dobles, principal of the Dual Language School, acknowledged the 
 school’s ten year anniversary and shared his school’s improvement plan for this year. 
 The Student Learning goal is, “By June 2027, students in every grade level will 
 increase their proficiency in the Language domain of the  Empowering Education 
 Writing Rubric (adapted for Dual Language Bilingual Education), as measured by 
 end-of-year benchmark writing assessments and monitored through quarterly 
 common formative assessments.” 
 Dual Language’s Professional Practice goal for this year is, “By the end of the 
 2026-2027 school year, DL staff will implement a systematic Tier II intervention 
 framework that uses consistent data collection, progress monitoring, and 
 collaborative analysis to identify student needs, monitor growth, and adjust literacy 
 and math interventions.” 
 The School Culture goal has been identified as, “By June 2027, 97% of students will 
 consistently demonstrate behaviors aligned with the school values, as evidenced by 
 meeting or exceeding the schoolwide proficiency benchmark on student 
 self-assessments and teacher feedback, supported by a reduction in behavior 
 incidents. The school values will be explicitly taught, modeled, practiced, and 
 celebrated schoolwide to support a positive and inclusive school culture.” 
 Dr. Dobles  shared the plans to achieve each of the stated goals and also how data 
 will monitor progress. 
 Nothing new was shared in this area. 
 Dr. Mendonsa advised she had a meeting with SMMA last week to review the ideas 
 for additional usage of the 617 Lexington Street building.  SMMA will review the 
 information and draft some proposed renovation plans. 
 There was nothing new shared in this category. 
 The superintendent advised work continues on the proposed high school schedule 
 options.  A conversation between Dr. Mendonsa, Mayor McCarthy and the members 
 ensued about sharing the proposals with the community prior to the forum, certain 
 non-negotiables that need to be included, community feedback, and the availability of 
 feedback data.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mayor McCarthy, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to forward the 
 three questions about the high school schedule posed during Public Comment to 
 WHS Principal Dr. Conard to be answered.  All in favor. 
 No new information was discussed. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Ms. Wong-Bigelow, seconded by Mrs. Coleman, to table this 
 matter to the next meeting.  All in favor. 
 There were no New Business matters on the agenda. 
 VOTED:  On  motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. DeJoannis, to approve the 
 three FY ‘27 account transfers.  All in favor. 
 Information was provided to the members by Administrator of Facilities Steve Jelloe 
 about the 617 Lexington Street Transformer Project.  Dr. Mendonsa advised that the 
 project encountered some unforeseen issues that needed to be addressed and the 
 funds originally allocated appear to have been depleted.  In order to co  mplete the 
 project, an additional $290,874.39 is needed. 
 Mayor McCarthy provided the members with information from the City Auditor’s office 
 detailing the funds recently expended relative to 617 Lexington Street.  She advised 
 it needs to be determined if the funds allocated for the replacement of a boiler and 
 the hot water valves were spent.  A short conversation about the scope of the 
 transformer project followed. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to pay the 
 bills on the warrant.  All in favor. 
 Mrs. AlJammal asked if alternative ways to earn physical education credits can be 
 explored as this might be beneficial when looking at proposed high school schedule 
 options. 
 Mayor McCarthy asked for information about the number of fights that have occurred 
 at Waltham High since the start of the year, the location of the fights, and the actions 
 being taken to prevent these situations from occurring in the future. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Ms. DeJoannis, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to adjourn 
 the Regular Meeting at 9:02pm.  All in favor. 
 Marisa Mendonsa 
 Clerk
